About Our Project

This project combines 2019 data from the Smart Location Database and Pedestrian Crash Data to provide a snapshot of how walkability infleunces multiple facets of life. Links to each database can be found below.

U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Smart Location Database (with Walkability Index)

https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/smart-location-database8

National Highway Safety Administration Pedestrian Crash Data

https://www.nhtsa.gov/file-downloads?p=nhtsa/downloads/FARS/

Employment

Completed by Cheyna Warner

Column

How does walkability impact employment rates?

Column

About

This plot shows the relationship between walkability and employment rates. Only data for capital cities is shown and only some capital cities were included in the dataset.

Research Question: How does walkability impact employment rates?

Hypothesis: I hypothesize that unemployment rates will be greater in less walkable areas.

Conclusions: Walkability and unemployment rates have a significant, negative relationship.

Cars

Completed by Cheyna Warner

Column

How does walkability impact the number of cars a household has?

Column

About

This graph shows the relationship between walkability and number of households that own at least 1 car. Only data for capital cities is shown and only some capital cities were included in the dataset.

Research Question: How does walkability impact the number of cars a household has?

Hypothesis: I hypothesize that people who live in walkable areas will have fewer cars.

Conclusions: Walkability and number of cars have a significant, positive relationship.
